Question design effects higher level cognitive processing as shown in a paper by 
(Richmond & Hagan, 2011). Within the study one group was taught using active 
learning techniques and the other with passive learning methods; student 
performance was gauged based off an exam with “high” and “low” level 
questions (refer to Table 1 for examples). The group that was taught using the 
active learning techniques significantly outperformed the passive learning group 
on the high-level questions, but the difference was not significant for the low-
level questions.  
In summary an effective assessment framework involves providing students with 
a tool to gauge their current level of understanding and a way of allowing the 
student to assess what they do not understand. The assessment should not just 
test students on facts, but on their deeper level of understanding, using high 
level questions. The level of complexity of these questions should be dependent 
on the student’s goals and skill level.
